doc.title: Genevieve Rose interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

title: Summer jazz workshops and favorite bassists
summary: Vermont Jazz Summer Workshop and Jazz in July shaped her; she names favorite bass recordings by Ray Brown and Ron Carter.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Was there a significant live performance along the way that you got to see, or a number of them that heightened your interest in the music? Seeing some well known musicians perhaps?
Well I think what definitely helped a lot was doing the jazz workshops in the summer. Like in the summer of ‘94 and ’95 I did the Vermont Jazz Summer Workshop, and that

was Attila Zoller’s Jazz Workshop, and also I did Jazz in July Workshops, Billy Taylor’s workshop there. And meeting all those musicians and it was kind of a hands on experience, that really helped a lot. And of course they’d have the concert so you could work with them. I’d say that was a very big influence there. Especially meeting people in person. That was always very important to me. But I can’t think off hand of a particular concert.
Well who has become your favorite bass players then?

Well I enjoy music from a lot of different bass players. I like some of Ray Brown, some of Ron Carter’s. There’s a bass player on one of Benny Waters’ CDs, Bob Bowman — no actually, I’m sorry, that’s Claude Williams’ CD, Bob Bowman. And I basically try to listen for specific recordings that I like. I don’t buy them just for the artist, but for that particular recording. Like for example I like Ron Carter on “Alone Together” with Jim Hall. So particular recordings, that’s what I look mostly for. And some of the bassists are no name bassists, and I just enjoy the way it sounds or a particular solo. But I look mostly at a particular recording rather than the artist themselves, for a variety.
